title: Monotonicity in the error bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\\{−1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and let $\\varepsilon,\\varepsilon',k\\in\\mathbb R$ with $\\varepsilon\\le\\varepsilon'$. If the sum of squared Fourier coefficients over coordinate sets whose size is strictly greater than $k$ is at most $\\varepsilon$, then that sum is at most $\\varepsilon'$ as well.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
